sentences.text: The captioned appeal is by the claimants, who are primarily aggrieved by the compensation determined by the Tribunal in MVC No.131/2019.
The respondent - insurance company admits its liability.
Appeal is purely on quantum.
Appellants/claimants are the son and widow of one Lachamappa, who died in a road traffic accident dated 02.05.2018.
The claim petition is filed asserting that Lachamappa while he was alive was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing coolie work and hence, filed a claim petition.
3. The Tribunal in absence of age proof, however placed reliance on the Aadhar Card, wherein, the date of birth of Lachamappa was shown as 01.01.1953.
Placing reliance on the Aadhar Card, the Tribunal proceeded to assess the age of the deceased as 68 years and accordingly, awarded Rs.4,70,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
The Tribunal in all awarded Rs.5,40,000/-.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants has vehemently argued and contended that Tribunal erred in relying on the date of birth indicated in Aadhar Card.
He would point out that age reflected in Aadhar Card cannot be relied upon and NC: 2024:KHC-K:9548 same is contrary to postmortem report, wherein, the deceased age was shown as 52 years.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent - Insurance Company would point out that the age reflected in Aadhar Card has evidentiary value and therefore, claimants themselves having placed reliance on Aadhar Card, cannot now claim that deceased was 52 years.
6. Heard learned counsels on record.
Perused the judgment under challenge.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants has furnished certified copy of the records.
The insurance company is banking heavily on admission elicited in the cross-examination of claimants.

The insurance company is also placing reliance on Aadhar Card, which is not marked,
but it appears that Xerox copy of the Aadhar Card is furnished by the insurance company.

Since there are conflicting documents relating to the age of the deceased, this Court in the absence of credible NC: 2024:KHC-K:9548 documents to determine the age of the deceased, is inclined to rely on postmortem report to ascertain the age of the deceased.

In the peculiar facts and circumstances,
this Court is also compelled to take cognizance of the age of the widow and son.
As on the date of the accident, widow is aged 40 years while son is hardly aged 22 years.
The postmortem report also reveals that deceased is shown to be aged 52 years as on the date of the accident.

Therefore, if these significant details are taken into consideration, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal's reliance on Xerox copy of the Aadhar Card to ascertain the age of the deceased appears to be fundamentally flawed.
8. Be that as it may.
The age indicated in the Aadhar car does not carry any credibility.
Often we have seen that the date of birth reflected in the Aadhar Card is not based on any supported documentary evidence before the entries are reflected in the Aadhar Card.

In the case on hand, it is not forthcoming whether deceased date of birth reflected in Aadhar Card was based on verified NC:
2024:KHC-K:9548 documents.
The age in the postmortem report is often an estimate made by forensic experts.
This estimation can have less margin of error, especially in adults.
Aadhar Cards are issued for identification purpose and therefore, the age reflected in the Aadhar Card cannot be taken as a credible information in regard to the date of birth.
9. On over all reassessing the records, this Court is compelled to assess the age of the deceased as 52 years as against 68 years.

If age is taken at 52 years and in the absence of income proof, income is assessed at Rs.11,750/- per month by placing reliance on the income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and 10% is added towards future prospects, income of the assessed is notionally assessed at Rs.12,925/-.
Since there are two dependents, 1/3rd needs to be deducted.

After deducting 1/3rd, income is atken at Rs.8,617/- per month and applying multiplier of 11, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.11,37,444/-
(Rs.8,617x12x11).
Under the conventional heads Rs.1,10,000/- is awarded.

By extending the benefit of escalation at the rate of 10% for every three years in the light of principles laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi1, an additional sum of Rs.22,000/- is paid on the conventional head at Rs.1,10,000/-.
